A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WeatherPrompt and are readable throughout, including their figures, tables, equations, references, and back matter. v1 ends with references; v3 adds acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate research appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original retrieval experiments on University-1652 and SUES-200, gating and prompting ablations, and evaluation on 54 drone-satellite video pairs collected from YouTube.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, qualitative retrieval examples, and real-world evaluation in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and Figure 4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same weather/spatial captioning pipeline, dynamic channel gating, alignment and classification losses, and inference procedure. The newly specified captioning-model size documents the existing method without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate University-1652 and SUES-200 in both retrieval directions under the same ten weather conditions, plus the same YouTube-derived adverse-weather evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: Tables 1–2 retain their backbone and retrieval-method rows, and Table 3c retains Sample4Geo and MuSe-Net. The new related-work citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same splits, 210-epoch SGD training schedule, image resizing and augmentation, Euclidean-distance retrieval, and recall/AP metrics. The checklist supplies additional disclosures rather than revising the reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same fusion-strategy ablation, no-caption and 0/2/4/6-step prompting comparisons, and real-world robustness evaluation. Figure 4 also retains the same qualitative retrieval examples.

E5.justification: v1 does not explain run counts or uncertainty reporting. v3 checklist item 7 newly describes following single-run, fixed-split benchmarking and explicitly explains the omission of error bars and significance metrics. This is additional reporting information, not evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes WeatherPrompt's SUES-200 drone-to-satellite R@1 under Over-exp from 81.60 to 61.57, without a reported setting change. This makes the ten weather-specific scores average to the retained 62.52. All other numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their mathematical definitions are substantively unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs; the new checklist merely acknowledges their absence.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: automatic CoT weather reasoning, language-guided scene/weather disentanglement through alignment and gating, and robust cross-weather geo-localization. Their scientific scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same interpretations of gating and prompting benefits and the same limitations concerning geographic/weather coverage and inherited language-model biases. The checklist's generic privacy and ethical caveats do not add a substantive scientific limitation or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a WeatherPrompt repository address, identifies Qwen2.5-VL-32B in checklist item 16, and states that hyperparameters were not delicately tuned. These are new disclosures; existing implementation details remain unchanged. Code availability is described inconsistently: the abstract says available, while the checklist promises a future release.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to A Discriminatively Learned CNN Embedding for Person Re-identification and Video2BEV, with a brief BEV mention. The broader research positioning remains unchanged; most other reference edits expand author lists or standardize bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, updates author and conference information, standardizes references, and adds acknowledgements and the checklist. The scientific sections retain their ordering and largely identical prose, without extensive narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 replace LLM/LMM labels with LVLM while retaining their diagrams. The author block is condensed, and figure/table spacing and page breaks change modestly. The same four figures and three scientific tables remain, with no substantial display redesign.

improvement.justification: The Table 2 revision resolves an arithmetic inconsistency with the reported 62.52 mean, while the model-size and single-run disclosures improve reproducibility and transparency. These are limited gains: Section 4.1 still gives a conflicting 61.20 mean, and the new code-release statements contradict each other. The underlying scientific study remains essentially unchanged.
